title: Close Update: Wall Street Surrenders Early Gains As Trade Hopes Dwindle
text:
Close Update: Wall Street Surrenders Early Gains As Trade Hopes Dwindle November 02, 2018, 04:38:31 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Wall Street's benchmark averages closed with a loss on Friday as hopes for a US/China trade deal evaporated and disappointing iPhone sales left Apple ( AAPL ) shares at their lowest level since August.
Despite bullish labor market data and trade jawboning by President Donald Trump, the Dow closed with a triple-digit loss but up 2.3% for the week. The S&P 500 was higher by 2.4% for the week, while the Nasdaq -- Friday's worst performing index -- closed out the week 2.6% higher and in the green for the first time since September.
US/China trade dominated market action Friday with comments from NEC head Larry Kudlow and President Trump jerking the Dow within a 400 point range.
The risk rally went into overdrive last night after Bloomberg claimed President Trump tasked his cabinet with putting together a trade deal with China. Kudlow said the reports were false but that Trump is planning to negotiate with Chinese president Xi Jinping next month at the G20 meeting. Later, Trump pulled stocks off their lows with assurances that a deal would be good for the US, allowing the Dow to cut its early losses in half.
The pivotal jobs report was nearly overshadowed by developments in Washington even as non-farm payrolls surged 250,000 in October and average hourly earnings rose by more than 3% year-over-year for the first time in more than nine years.
Additionally, factory orders jumped 0.7% in October, following an upwardly revised 2.6% gain the month prior, and the US trade deficit swelled to $54.0 billion as imports and the trade deficit with China set record highs.
